critical_code_review_comments: JobPicker.jsx line 117 uses document.querySelector('[cmdk-list=""]') which resolves the FIRST cmdk-list in the document. If multiple JobPicker popovers or other cmdk lists could ever be open simultaneously, the scroll listener could attach to the wrong list. Not a bug today (only one picker open at a time), but a scoped ref (e.g. querying inside the PopoverContent DOM node) would be more defensive.

The dx/dy secondary guard at line 151-155 relies on synthesized clientX/clientY at pointerup — on real iOS Safari touch scrolls, pointerup may fire with the final position which is fine, but if pointerup is missing entirely due to a pointercancel, the primary scrolledRef guard still handles it via onPointerCancel. Coverage looks complete.
Consider adding a data-testid on [cmdk-list] element itself (e.g. data-testid='job-picker-list') to avoid coupling test/query code to cmdk's internal attribute schema.
context_for_next_testing_agent: JobPicker.jsx now uses a container-level native scroll listener on [cmdk-list=''] with scrolledRef.current to distinguish scroll from tap.
